subject: home-science
title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 2½ hours · Maximum marks: 85 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–19 are MCQs (1 mark each); questions 20–31 are objective questions of 2 marks each.
Section B: questions 32–41 carry 2 marks (30–50 words), questions 42–45 carry 3 marks (50–80 words) and questions 46–47 carry 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: Match the columns: (A) Communication and extension (B) Housekeeping (C) Interior decorator (D) Dress designing; (i) Boutique (ii) Media production and management (iii) Staff at hotels (iv) Furniture designer.

Fill in the blanks: (i) Khichri is an example of ______ method of enhancement. (ii) Milk polybags should not be exposed to sunlight as vitamin ______ gets lost. (iii) Quality of oil becomes ______ when it is reheated repeatedly. (iv) During frying, the temperature of oil becomes ______ degrees C.

State True or False: (i) Milk is heated to a high temperature and immediately cooled to kill its germs. (ii) Increasing the concentration of acid can lead to food spoilage. (iii) Citric acid is used as a preservative. (iv) Low temperature slows down microbial action.
questions.answer: (i) True (pasteurisation). (ii) False – more acid prevents spoilage. (iii) True. (iv) True.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Loud noise can damage hearing. (ii) Burning of refuse is banned in metros. (iii) Fish die in polluted water because less oxygen is available. (iv) Latrines should be built close to water sources.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – they should be far from water sources.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Diabetes and hypertension are ______ diseases. (ii) Plenty of fluids and ______ should be given in dehydration. (iii) Obesity is excess ______ than the ideal for height. (iv) Age and heredity are ______ factors.

State True or False: (i) Laundering is the same as washing. (ii) Airing of clothes helps when they are not to be washed at once. (iii) Stains should be removed before washing. (iv) Synthetics should be squeezed well before drying.
questions.answer: (i) False – it includes washing or dry cleaning, finishing and storing. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – squeezing makes them wrinkle; dry on a hanger.

questions.q: Match the finish with the chemical or equipment: (I) Mercerisation (II) Parchmentisation (III) Calendering (IV) Bleaching; (a) Hot rollers (b) Sodium hypochlorite (c) Sodium hydroxide (d) Mild acid.

Fill in the blanks: (i) Besides windows, doors and ventilators, ______ should be installed in the kitchen to remove stale air. (ii) Chances of infections and fungal diseases increase if the rooms are ______. (iii) The floor of a bathroom should be ______. (iv) The living room should be near the ______ of the building.
questions.answer: (i) an exhaust fan. (ii) dark and damp. (iii) non-slippery. (iv) entrance.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) All activities should be listed before time planning. (ii) Shopping is an inflexible activity. (iii) Balancing is adjustment of time for each activity. (iv) A time plan should not be changed.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False – shopping is flexible. (iii) True. (iv) False – a time plan should be flexible.

Match the vaccine with the disease: (i) BCG (ii) Oral polio (iii) DPT (iv) MMR; (a) diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus (b) polio (c) tuberculosis (d) measles, mumps, rubella.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name the two fastest methods of cooking and write two drawbacks of a solar cooker.
questions.answer: Pressure cooking and microwave cooking are the fastest. A solar cooker works only when there is plenty of sunshine and can only be used outdoors.

questions.q: Why are green leafy vegetables not put in KMS solution before drying?
questions.answer: Potassium metabisulphite bleaches the colour of green leafy and other dark vegetables, so they lose their natural colour.

questions.q: Suggest four efforts that people can make to reduce noise pollution in their society.
questions.answer: Play radio and TV at low volume; avoid loudspeakers; blow vehicle horns only when necessary; fit silencers in vehicles; talk in low tones; build factories and airports away from residential areas (any four).

questions.q: List any four myths regarding the spread of HIV/AIDS.
questions.answer: HIV does not spread by shaking hands, kissing on the cheek, using the same toilet seat, standing close to or sitting with the infected person, sneezing or coughing, sharing cups, glasses and plates, or through food and water.

or.q: Write four causes of increase in lifestyle diseases.
or.answer: Junk and processed food; less physical activity (use of vehicles and machines); smoking and drinking; stress; overeating and obesity; replacement of milk and fresh fruits by soft drinks and packed foods.

questions.q: List four steps involved in the process of laundering clothes.
questions.answer: Soaking, washing, rinsing, finishing (starching or blueing), drying, ironing and storing (any four).

questions.q: Why is a mercerised fabric preferred? Give two advantages.
questions.answer: Mercerisation with sodium hydroxide makes cotton strong, lustrous and absorbent, and it improves dye uptake; sewing threads are mercerised too.

questions.q: Write any four educational functions of a house.
questions.answer: It teaches basic values like respect for elders, love and affection, religion, discipline and responsibility; life skills like sharing, caring and empathy; health habits; and transfers customs and values from generation to generation.

or.q: List any four household activities that are done once a week in your home.
or.answer: Cleaning bathrooms and toilets; removing cobwebs; cleaning kitchen shelves; cleaning door handles; polishing wooden surfaces; cleaning washbasins and metal objects.

questions.q: By dovetailing, the work of cooking dal, cooking vegetables, washing dishes and washing clothes (20 minutes each) was finished in 55 minutes. How much time was saved?
questions.answer: Without dovetailing: 20 + 20 + 20 + 20 = 80 minutes. With dovetailing: 55 minutes. Time saved = 80 – 55 = 25 minutes.

questions.q: Families are not able to meet their needs with rising inflation. Suggest four ways to cut their expenses.
questions.answer: Avoid wasting food and eating out; save electricity and water; use public transport or a cycle; iron and wash clothes at home; use stationery economically; borrow from the public library; look out for sales and shop in one trip; avoid impulsive buying.

or.q: Prepare a format to record one month food expenses of your family.
or.answer: A table headed Month and Year with rows for cereals, pulses, vegetables, fruits, milk, ghee/oil, spices, egg/meat and others, columns for Week 1, Week 2, Week 3 and Week 4, and a Total column for each item and for the month.

questions.q: As an Asha worker make the women aware of four signs that confirm pregnancy.
questions.answer: Missed menstrual period; morning sickness or nausea; enlarged, tender breasts with darker nipple area; frequent urination; cravings for or aversion to certain foods.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Why do you wash cotton clothes in soapy water, rinse and starch them? Write the steps of laundering white cotton clothes (any six).
questions.answer: (1) Sort and mend. (2) Remove stains. (3) Soak white cottons in warm water for up to half an hour. (4) Wash in soap solution – light clothes by kneading, heavy ones with a stick, very dirty parts with hand or brush. (5) Rinse at least three times and add blue. (6) Starch for a smooth, fresh look and dry in the sun; iron when damp; store when completely dry.

questions.q: Your family is always short of time. Tell your family members six benefits of making a time plan.
questions.answer: You finish work efficiently without feeling tired; get time for rest; get time for hobbies; do more productive work in less time; are saved from last-minute tension and confusion; get time for unforeseen events like guests or illness; the quality of work improves.

questions.q: What is the role of parents towards infants, school-going children and adolescents?
questions.answer: Infants: feeding, loving, clothing, bathing, immunisation and early stimulation. School-going children: support in studies, a separate study space, group games and good eating habits. Adolescents: set rules and limits, be firm and flexible, keep communication open, trust them, give emotional support and help them prepare for a career.

questions.q: Write any six characteristic features of a good label of a food product.
questions.answer: Name of the product and brand; manufacturer's name and address; ingredients; date of manufacture and date of expiry; net weight; MRP; directions for use and storage; standard mark (Agmark, FPO, ISI); lot or batch number; guarantee or warnings.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps of making a spending plan and the factors on which allocation of money to different items depends.
questions.answer: Steps: keep in mind all income and facilities; list all requirements; prioritise needs; allocate funds according to total income; balance the plan (earn more or cut expenses) and keep records. Allocation depends on income of the family, size of the family, age of family members (school-going children), place of residence (cost of living is higher in big cities), skills of members and the amount to be saved (about 10%).

questions.q: Write any five physical changes in adolescent girls.
questions.answer: Increase in height and weight; growth of breasts; broadening of hips; growth of underarm and pubic hair; pimples or acne; development of reproductive organs; menarche (start of menstruation).

or.q: Suggest any five ways to develop self-esteem in adolescents.
or.answer: Accept strong points and appreciate them; acknowledge weaknesses and work on them; accept physical aspects that cannot be changed; avoid self-pity; seek advice from a trusted friend, parent or counsellor; appreciate others honestly; eat healthy and exercise; take pride in abilities and success.
